title: D$^3$S$^2$: Diffusion-Guided Dataset Distillation for Semantic Segmentation
claim: Prior distillation methods match gradients or statistics and ignore dense-label needs and long-tailed classes; ours synthesizes images from balanced masks via diffusion.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, color-coded dashed boxes, class histograms at right
description: Four dashed-border panels read left to right. The left column is split into two stacked panels with a blue border. (a) shows a data-matching framework: an initialized classifier is applied to synthetic and original image sets, and a match loss compares gradients, distributions or trajectories. (b) shows a decoupled framework: a pretrained network supplies global and local batch-norm statistics, which feed a regularization loss that updates the synthetic set. The orange middle panel (c) is the proposed method, drawn as a two-stage pipeline. Stage I takes a long-tailed pool of colorful segmentation masks and uses class-balanced greedy selection to produce a diverse mask set. Stage II feeds the mask and noise into a layout-to-image diffusion model with a segmentor providing guided sampling, producing a synthesized image. The green right panel (d) holds two pairs of bar charts for ADE20K and COCO-Stuff, each with a head-class bar and a tail-class bar. Red arrows mark the extreme imbalance factors. The eye goes first to the large central panel.
caption: (a) Data-matching methods; (b) Decoupled methods; (c) Our proposed D3S2, the first DD framework tailored for semantic segmentation, which generates distilled data via a layout-to-image diffusion model; (d) Class distributions of ADE20K [59] and COCO-Stuff [2].
abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress large-scale datasets into compact synthetic sets while preserving training efficacy. However, existing studies mainly focus on image classification, leaving dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation largely underexplored. In this work, we identify three key challenges for segmentation DD: (i) long-tailed class imbalance, (ii) the need for strict pixel-wise alignment between images and dense labels, and (iii) the high computational cost of optimizing high-resolution data with complex models. To address these challenges, we propose D3S2, a Diffusion-guided Dataset Distillation framework for Semantic Segmentation. Our method adopts a two-stage design. In Class-Balanced Mask Selection, we construct a representative mask set via a greedy strategy that prioritizes underrepresented classes. In Diffusion-Guided Image Synthesis, we employ a pretrained layout-to-image diffusion model to generate images conditioned on the selected masks, naturally ensuring spatial alignment. To further enhance the training utility of synthesized data, we introduce guided diffusion sampling with two complementary objectives: a segmentation-consistency loss for pixel-level alignment, and a class-wise feature matching loss for aligning per-class feature statistics across layers. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of D3S2. Notably, at an extremely compression rate of 1%, our method achieves 24.99% and 35.49% mIoU on ADE20K and COCO-Stuff with Mask2Former (Swin-S), outperforming random selection by 9.34% and 5.70%, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/zwj084/D3S2.
